title: Trump Unhinged: Goes After Mexico at UN – Soberanía 125
author: Mexico Solidarity
content:
In episode 125 of Soberanía, hosts José Luis Granados Ceja and Kurt Hackbarth
open with Trump's speech at the UN General Assembly, where he called Mexico
"the epicenter of cartel violence," threatened to "annihilate" Iran, and
declared Cuba a failed state. They highlight President Sheinbaum's sharp
response: "It's also difficult to live next to a country with high drug
consumption and arms production." They also discuss the Special Rapporteur's
report condemning the U.S. boat bombings as extrajudicial executions, and the
growing push to invoke the Rio Treaty to militarize the hemisphere through the
so-called "Shield of the Americas."

Next, they examine the controversy over Morena's candidate selection process
for the 2027 gubernatorial elections. With no primaries, the party uses
opinion polling — which inherently favors those with high name recognition and
disadvantages emerging candidates. The result: several candidates with ties to
the old PRI, PRD, or PAN, raising questions about their commitment to the
Fourth Transformation. The hosts debate the challenges of every option —
primaries are costly and traumatized by the PRD experience, assemblies can be
stacked with "acarreados," and polls reward incumbents — concluding that while
it's a difficult dilemma, Morena's new leadership under Adriana Montiel faces
a credibility test.

The episode also covers the U.S. Embassy's disastrous attempt to attack China
on Mexico's Independence Day, tweeting that Mexican patriotic symbols are
"made in China." China's response was sharp and dignified: "A nation's
Independence Day belongs to its people." A poll showed 58% of Mexicans see the
U.S. as a threat, compared to 27% who see China as one.

Losers and Haters takes aim at historian Enrique Krauze, who shared a video of
Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco at an LGBTQ+ event at the UN and called it
"the lowest point in Mexican diplomacy in 200 years" — a comment the hosts
condemn as homophobic and historically illiterate, noting far worse examples
from Mexico's diplomatic past.
